# Component guide

One entry per component, copied from the design system. Props and types are in `packages/ui-web/src/index.d.ts`. For a live view of every component, open the design system gallery.

## Button

Group: Actions

Use Button for every action. Default is `secondary` (outlined); use `primary` (`light-blue` fill) at most once per screen, for the action the screen exists for.

- Provide: `children` (a verb first, plain words: "Send credits"), `onClick` or `type="submit"`.
- Member screens use `size="lg"` (52px tall) and an `icon` beside the label; never an icon alone.
- `size="sm"` only in manager tables and toolbars; `ghost` for low-weight actions; `danger` for suspending or closing.
- While an action runs, disable the button and change its label ("Sending…").

## TextField

Group: Forms

Use TextField for single-line input, always with a visible `label`.

- Provide: `label`, `value`/`onChange` (or `defaultValue`), and native input props.
- Member screens set `large`. Put the unit in `suffix` ("credits") so people type only the number.
- `hint` says what to type or what is available; `error` replaces it with an icon and a plain sentence of what to do.

## PasswordField

Group: Forms

Use PasswordField for a password, with a visible `label` and a Show/Hide button so people can check what they typed.

- Provide: `label`, `value`/`onChange`, and `autoComplete`: `"current-password"` to sign in, `"new-password"` to set a password. Password managers rely on it.
- Ask for a new password once. The Show button replaces a second "repeat the password" field.
- Put the rule in `hint` ("At least 12 characters."). The backend checks it and returns the message for `error`.
- Never paste-block the field and never clear it after a wrong attempt on another field.

## Select

Group: Forms

Use Select to pick one value from a short fixed list (up to about 10 options).

- Provide: `label`, `options` (strings or `{value, label}`), `value`/`onChange` or `defaultValue`.
- `placeholder` adds a disabled first option; pair it with `defaultValue=""`.
- Same `hint`/`error` behaviour as TextField.

## Textarea

Group: Forms

Use Textarea for text longer than one line, such as a description or a note, always with a visible `label`.

- Provide: `label`, `value`/`onChange` (or `defaultValue`), and native textarea props such as `rows` and `maxLength`.
- Say in `hint` what to write and how long it may be ("Up to 500 characters").
- Member screens set `large`.

## DateField

Group: Forms

Use DateField to pick one day with the browser's own date picker, always with a visible `label`.

- Provide: `label`, `value` and `onChange` (the value is "YYYY-MM-DD"), and `min`/`max` when only some days are allowed.
- The browser shows the date in the reader's format and keeps the picker accessible.
- For a period with a start and an end, use DateRangeField.

## DateRangeField

Group: Forms

Use DateRangeField to pick a period with a start day and an end day, under one label.

- Provide: `label`, `value` (`{ from, to }`, each "YYYY-MM-DD") and `onChange`. `min` and `max` limit both days.
- The end cannot be before the start: each picker limits the other.
- Put it in the filter row above charts and tables, next to a period Select when there are preset periods.

## Checkbox

Group: Forms

Use Checkbox for one yes-or-no choice that the person confirms with the form, such as "Send an invitation email".

- Provide: `label`, `checked`/`onChange` (or `defaultChecked`). The label says what happens when it is ticked.
- For a setting that applies at once, use Switch. For one choice from several, use RadioGroup.
- Member screens set `large`.

## RadioGroup

Group: Forms

Use RadioGroup to choose one option from two to five, all visible at once.

- Provide: `label` (the question), `options` (`{ value, label, description? }`), and `value`/`onChange` or `defaultValue`.
- Put a short `description` under an option when its effect is not obvious, for example what a role may do.
- For longer lists, use Select. Member screens set `large`.

## Switch

Group: Forms

Use Switch for a setting that is either on or off, such as "Account active" or "Email alerts".

- Provide: `label`, `checked`/`onChange` (or `defaultChecked`). The current state is also written beside the label ("On", "Off", or your own `onLabel`/`offLabel`).
- A Switch applies its setting at once, or with the form it belongs to: say which in the `hint` when it is not clear.
- Ask for confirmation in a Dialog before a switch takes access away from someone.

## Dialog

Group: Forms

Use Dialog for a short task that needs the person's full attention, such as a form to invite a user or a confirmation before an action that is hard to undo.

- Provide: `open`, `title`, `onClose`, `actions` (the buttons) and `children` (the content).
- Put the cancel button first and the main action last. The main action is a verb ("Invite user", "Deactivate"); use `variant="danger"` for an action that takes something away.
- The Dialog keeps focus inside, closes on Escape and hides the page behind it. Its content is created each time it opens, so a form inside starts empty.
- Keep it short: one task, no tabs, no second Dialog on top. A long form gets its own page.

## Card

Group: Layout

Use Card to group one topic on a dashboard or detail page; its title carries the manual's short green rule.

- Provide: `title`, `children`; optionally `subtitle`, `actions` (small buttons, top right) and `footer` (metadata on `surface-muted`).
- Set `flush` when the body is a DataTable, AccountList or TransactionList so rows run edge to edge.
- Place cards on `surface-muted`; cards themselves are `surface` with a `line` border and square corners, no shadow.

## Badge

Group: Status

Use Badge for a one- or two-word status beside a name or amount, mostly in manager screens.

- Provide: `children` (the word; colour never carries meaning alone) and `tone`: `success` (active, certified), `info` (measured, information), `warning` (estimated), `danger` (suspended), `neutral` (closed, manual).
- Text stays `ink` on the tinted grounds; only `danger` uses `danger` text.
- On member screens prefer a plain sentence or `InlineAlert` over a badge.

## InlineAlert

Group: Status

Use InlineAlert to tell people something important on the page: an outcome, a warning, or why something did not work.

- Provide: `tone` (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `error`), a short `title` and one plain sentence as `children`.
- Every tone has an icon and a border, so colour is never the only signal.
- Errors say what happened and what to do; after a failed send, say that no credits moved (the ledger rolls back any failed operation).

## Icon

Group: Status

Use Icon beside words to help people recognise an action or kind of activity at a glance.

- Provide: `name`. Icons are decorative by default; give `label` only when an icon stands alone, which member screens should avoid.
- The set is small and original: sun, wind, plug, battery, clock, wallet, coins, panel, wrench, heart, star, exchange, arrows, person, check, info, alert, search, chevron, back.
- Use `wallet` for wallets and accounts, and `coins` for credits and investments.
- Icons inherit the text colour.

## StatTile

Group: Dashboard

Use StatTile for one headline number on a manager dashboard, in a row of two to four.

- Provide: `label`, `value`, `unit`. Negative values show a minus sign.
- `accent` colours the top bar: `green` for energy figures, `light-blue` for platform and wallet figures, `orange` for community activity, following the manual's colour associations.
- `delta` adds a change line with an arrow and a word label.

## DataTable

Group: Dashboard

Use DataTable for rows of records with aligned columns.

- Provide: `columns` (`key`, `header`, optional `align: "right"` for numbers, optional `render`) and `rows`; `rowKey` names the id field (default `id`).
- `onRowClick` makes rows keyboard-focusable and clickable; `selectedKey` highlights a row in `light-blue-tint`.
- Right-align all quantities and include the unit in the cell.
- Give `emptyText` that says what will appear ("No member accounts yet.").

## Identifier

Group: Ledger

Use Identifier to show a wallet ID, transaction ID or hash in manager and support screens. Never show identifiers on member screens outside "Technical details".

- Provide: `value`; optional `label` names it for the Copy button ("transaction ID").
- Shortened by default with the full value on hover; `full` shows all of it.

## PurposeTag

Group: Ledger

Use PurposeTag to say what kind of activity a movement was. Members see an icon and plain words; managers can see the raw code.

- Provide: `code` (a purpose_code) or `txType`, and `direction` (`in` or `out`) so the wording fits ("Solar energy you shared", "Community energy you used").
- `technical` shows the raw code (`GEN_SOLAR`) for manager tables.
- The plain wording is a proposal and should be checked with members.

## ConfidenceBadge

Group: Ledger

Use ConfidenceBadge in manager and support screens to show how trustworthy the data behind a transaction is.

- Provide: `level`: `CERTIFIED`, `MEASURED`, `ESTIMATED` or `MANUAL`. The tooltip explains each in one line.
- Members see only "Estimated reading" where it applies, not this badge.

## WalletBalance

Group: Member

Use WalletBalance as the first thing a member sees: how many credits they have.

- Provide: `balance` (from the backend). Optional `available` if the backend reports a different spendable amount, `updated` (already formatted) and `actions` (large buttons: "Send credits", "Exchange").
- The number is large (48px) with the word "credits"; nothing else competes with it.
- A balance below zero is shown with a minus sign in the normal text colour, never red. Pass `negativeNote` with a plain explanation from the backend.

## BalanceStatement

Group: Member

Use BalanceStatement to show a member what changed in a period: the balance at the start, each kind of activity, and the balance at the end.

- Provide: `period`, `opening`, `closing` and `lines` (`direction`, `purposeCode` or `txType`, `amount`, optional `count`). All values come from the backend.
- Group many movements of one kind into one line with `count` rather than listing each.

## EnergySummary

Group: Member

Use EnergySummary to connect a member's electricity with their credits for a period.

- Provide: `used` (`communityKwh`, `supplierKwh`, optional `credits` and `supplierNote`) and optional `shared` (`kWh`, `credits`).
- It shows kWh and credit amounts only, never conversion factors or formulas; the backend computes the credits.
- Set `estimated` when any reading in the period was estimated.

## TransactionList

Group: Member

Use TransactionList for a member's recent activity, newest first.

- Provide: `transactions` (each with `direction`, `amount` and `purposeCode` or `txType`; `counterpartyName` for member-to-member transfers; `time` already formatted).
- Each row is an icon, one plain sentence, the date and a signed amount. Set `onSelect` to make whole rows open TransactionDetail (rows are at least 64px tall).
- Ledger records are final once written, so there is no "pending" or "failed" state here.

## TransactionDetail

Group: Member

Use TransactionDetail when a member or manager opens one movement.

- Provide: `transaction`. The top shows the amount and what it was in plain words, then when, who, energy and note.
- The full ledger record (IDs, wallets, purpose code, valuation rule, metering point, data quality, hashes) sits in a closed "Technical details" section for managers and support. Set `showTechnical={false}` to hide it entirely.

## RecipientPicker

Group: Member

Use RecipientPicker to choose who receives credits: a searchable list of people, never a typed address.

- Provide: `recipients` (`id` of the receiving wallet, `name`, optional `detail` such as a street) from the backend, `value`, `onChange`.
- Rows are 60px tall with initials, name and detail. Mark people who cannot receive with `disabled`.
- Which names and details members may see of each other is a privacy decision for the backend.

## TransferForm

Group: Member

Use TransferForm to send credits to another member in three steps: choose a person, enter an amount, check and send.

- Provide: `recipients`, `available` (from the backend), `onSubmit({ to, amount, note })`.
- Report progress with `status`: `working` while the backend acts, `done` with `newBalance`, or `error` with the backend's `errorCode` or your own `errorMessage`. `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE` has its own message and other codes show a generic one; every error message ends by saying that no credits moved.
- The check step shows the amount and the person, not the balance after the send: only the backend computes balances. The result screen shows `newBalance` as the backend reports it.
- The form checks only that the amount is above zero and not above `available`. All other rules (limits, minimum balances, eligibility) are the backend's.

## SettlementRequestForm

Group: Member

Use SettlementRequestForm when a member asks to exchange credits for money. It sends a request; it does not move credits.

- Provide: `available`, `onSubmit({ amount })`; optional `estimate(credits)` returning a formatted money amount when the backend can give one.
- The confirmation says the community manager must approve and that payment happens outside the app.
- Report progress with `status` as for TransferForm.

## AccountCard

Group: Manager

Use AccountCard in manager screens for one member and their wallets.

- Provide: `member` with `name`, `role`, `status` and `wallets` (`id`, `type`, `balance`, `status`, optional `label`).
- Balances are in EC with a minus sign when below zero; community and dependent wallets are normally below zero.
- `actions`: small buttons such as History and Suspend.

## AccountList

Group: Manager

Use AccountList in manager screens to list wallets with owner, type, ID, balance and status.

- Provide: `wallets` (`id`, `name`, `type`: `MEMBER`, `COMMUNITY` or `DEPENDENT`, `balance`, `status`: `ACTIVE`, `SUSPENDED` or `CLOSED`).
- `onSelect` + `selectedId` turn it into a master list for AccountCard.

## TopBar

Group: Shell

Use TopBar at the top of every INNO-TREC web tool.

- Provide: `logoSrc` (use `assets/Logos/logo-landscape-colour.png` on this white bar), `title` (the tool's name), optional `user` (`{name, role}`) and `actions`.
- Keep the logo at 32px tall; its clearspace (height ÷ 4 = 8px) is covered by the bar's padding.

## SideNav

Group: Shell

Use SideNav for a tool's main navigation.

- Provide: `items` or `sections` (`[{title, items: [{id, label, href?, icon?}]}]`), `activeId`, `onNavigate`.
- Member apps: four or five items at most, each with an `icon` and a plain label ("My credits", "Send credits", "History").
- The current item gets `aria-current="page"` and a highlighted row. Under 720px wide it becomes a horizontal row.

## Footer

Group: Shell

Use Footer at the bottom of every INNO-TREC web tool to show the EU funding emblem, the funding statement and the legal links.

- Provide: `emblemSrc` (the negative emblem, `assets/Funding/eu-funded-negative.png`, because the footer ground is `ink`) and `links` (at least the tool's privacy policy).
- The funding statement for the Horizon Europe grant (agreement 101230578) is built in. Replace it with `funding` only when the funding changes, and keep the EU wording.
- Pass it to AppShell as `footer`; it then spans the full width under the side navigation and the main area.
- Use the colour emblem; the monochrome versions are only for places where colour is not possible. Never recolour, crop or redraw it, and keep it at least as tall as any other logo on the page (48px here, the top-bar logo is 32px).
- No social media links in a tool footer.

## AppShell

Group: Shell

Use AppShell as the page frame of an INNO-TREC web tool: TopBar, SideNav, a main area on `surface-muted` and an optional Footer.

- Provide: `logoSrc`, `title`, `user`, `navItems` or `navSections`, `activeId`, `onNavigate`, `heading` (the page's h1) and `children` (the page content, usually Cards and StatTiles).
- Pass a Footer as `footer`. It sits below the side navigation and the main area, and the main area grows so the footer stays at the bottom of the window.
- Give the shell a full-height parent (`height: 100%` on html and body) so the side navigation runs to the bottom.

## AuthLayout

Group: Shell

Use AuthLayout as the frame of every screen without a session: sign in, create an account, accept an invitation, reset a password.

- Provide: `logoSrc` and `title` (as in AppShell), `heading` (the screen's h1), an optional `intro`, the form as `children`, and the same `Footer` as the signed-in screens.
- One task per screen, with one primary button. Put the way to the other screen in `aside` ("New here? Create an account").
- Say what went wrong without helping an attacker: "The email or password is wrong", not which one. After a reset request, show the same message whether the email exists or not.
- The panel is 440px wide at most and fills the width on a phone. Use the standard field size; members' screens may set `large`.

## EmptyState

Group: Status

Use EmptyState when a whole section or page has nothing to show yet: no alerts, no users, no readings in a period.

- Provide: `title` (what is missing: "No alerts yet"), one sentence as `children` (when something will appear, or what to do), and an optional `action` with the Button that adds the first item.
- Say why it is empty when the page knows it. After a filter, say "Choose another filter to see more alerts", not only "Nothing found".
- Use `plain` and `level={3}` inside a Card. An empty table inside a DataTable uses its `emptyText` instead.
- An empty state is not an error. When loading fails, show an `InlineAlert` with `tone="error"` and a "Try again" button.

## Tabs

Group: Layout

Use Tabs to switch between views of the same content on one page, for example alerts by state (Open, Resolved, All) or the sections of an asset.

- Provide: `tabs` (`id`, `label`, and an optional `count` from the backend), `activeId` and `onChange`. The page keeps the active tab; put it in the address when people share links to it.
- Give the list a `label` for screen readers ("Alerts by state"). The arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs.
- Two to six tabs, with short labels. More choices, or choices that combine, go in a `Select`.
- Not for steps (use a step flow with Back) and not for links to other pages (use the side navigation).
- Pass the active view as `children`, or render it below the Tabs yourself.

## Pagination

Group: Dashboard

Use Pagination below a long list that the backend sends in pages.

- Provide: `page` (starting at 1), `pageSize`, `total` from the backend and `onChange`. A backend that does not count sends whether another page exists: pass `hasNext` instead of `total`.
- Set `itemLabel` ("alerts") so the count reads "1–10 of 42 alerts".
- Put it in the `footer` of the Card that holds the DataTable. It renders nothing when the whole list fits on one page.
- Go back to page 1 when a filter or tab changes. The backend counts and pages the list; the interface never counts rows it did not receive.

## Toast

Group: Status

Use Toast to confirm that a change was saved, after the dialog or form that made it has closed: "Alert resolved", "Invitation sent to ana@example.org".

- Provide: `open`, `onClose` and one sentence as `children`. It closes by itself after 6 seconds (`duration`) and waits while the pointer or the keyboard focus is on it. It also has a Dismiss button.
- Errors are never a toast. Show them next to the form or the section, where they stay until the person acts.
- Do not put the only copy of important information in a toast. If people need it later (a link, a code), show it on the page.
- One toast at a time. A new message replaces the previous one. An optional `action` holds one small button, for example "Undo".
- Render it once per page. It sits at the bottom of the window and announces the message to screen readers.

## FileUpload

Group: Forms

Use FileUpload to attach files to a form, for example photos of a repair. People choose files with the button or drop them on the field.

- Provide: `label`, `files` (the list the page keeps: `name`, `size`), `onAdd` and `onRemove`. Set `multiple` to allow more than one file.
- Say in `hint` what to attach and the limits ("Photos of the work, up to 10 MB each."). `accept` filters the browser's picker, but the backend checks the type and size and returns the message for `error`, or for one file in its `error`.
- Files sent with the form need no status. Files sent at once show `status`: Uploading…, Uploaded or Not uploaded.
- Keep the chosen files after a failed submit, so people do not choose them again.
